title: Snap Beats Q2 Expectations, Opens Preorders for $2,195 AR Glasses
excerpt: Revenue rose 19% to $1.6 billion on direct-response advertising strength and World Cup spending, while the company's Spectacles bet targets developers over consumers.
body:
• Snap reported Q2 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 19% year-over-year and ahead of the $1.54 billion Wall Street consensus, driven by direct-response advertising and a World Cup ad spending boost.
  • Net loss narrowed to $0.10 per share from $0.15 a year ago, with daily active users hitting 493 million, up 5%.
  • The company opened preorders for its fifth-generation Spectacles AR glasses at $2,195, positioning the hardware as a developer and early-adopter product rather than a mass-market device.
  • Q3 revenue guidance of $1.70–1.74 billion exceeded analyst expectations, sending shares up roughly 10% in after-hours trading.

The Numbers

Snap delivered a quarter that beat expectations across the board. Revenue came in at $1.6 billion, up 19% from a year earlier and comfortably above the $1.54 billion analysts had projected. The company's net loss narrowed to $0.10 per share from $0.15 in the year-ago quarter, continuing a slow but steady march toward profitability.

Daily active users reached 493 million, a 5% increase year-over-year, with growth concentrated in developing markets. The user base now spans more than 40 countries, with India remaining one of Snapchat's fastest-growing markets — a dynamic that has made the platform increasingly relevant for Indian diaspora advertising and cultural commerce.

What Drove the Beat

Snap credited two forces for the revenue outperformance: continued improvements in its direct-response advertising platform, and a boost from the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which drove incremental ad spending from major brands. Direct-response ads — the kind that ask users to swipe up, install an app, or make a purchase — now generate the majority of Snap's revenue, a shift that has made the business less dependent on the brand-awareness campaigns that dried up during the 2023 downturn.

The company also noted strong momentum in its Snapchat+ subscription service, which now has more than 14 million paying subscribers, though it did not break out subscription revenue separately.

"We are in the early innings of what we believe is a multi-year opportunity to grow our advertising platform."

— Evan Spiegel, CEO, Snap Inc.

The Spectacles Bet

Snap used the earnings report to announce preorders for its fifth-generation Spectacles, the company's augmented reality glasses, at a price point of $2,195. The glasses feature an improved field of view, longer battery life, and deeper integration with Snap's Lens Studio developer tools.

At that price, Spectacles are not a consumer product — they're a developer platform. Snap is betting that by getting AR glasses into the hands of creators and enterprise customers early, it can build the software ecosystem necessary for a future mass-market product. The strategy mirrors Meta's approach with its Quest headsets, though at a fraction of Meta's hardware investment.

Looking Ahead

Snap's Q3 revenue guidance of $1.70–1.74 billion came in above the $1.68 billion analysts had expected, signaling continued advertising momentum into the second half of the year. Shares rose approximately 10% in after-hours trading on the results.

The company faces a familiar set of challenges: competition from TikTok and Instagram for younger users' attention, regulatory uncertainty around data privacy, and the capital-intensive nature of its AR hardware ambitions. But for now, the advertising business is performing, the user base is growing, and investors are rewarding the execution.
